explanation: The first ship to the settlement carried six enslaved Africans among sixty-odd settlers, and about forty enslaved Taíno were brought from Guyana to plant. The scale is the whole difference from what came after: before 1650 more than three quarters of the islands’ population was of European descent, and by 1680 the median Barbadian estate held sixty enslaved people. The colony is where the traffic landed; it is not why it grew.
